# EASA kit · 08 — Any aircraft: how many sensors does a latch with N points need? (generated by `easa_kit.py`)

**Question it answers** (mentor Q2, "pick your example aircraft (any)"): does LOCK-SENSE transfer to a type with a different number of latch points (pins, shoot bolts, hooks)?

**Model [K]:** the Extra NG study (`aerokit.canopy.montecarlo`) with the number of latch points changed and everything else kept: channel rates, rigging tolerances, 60→70 mm handle-equivalent travel, exposure and nuisance rate from `02_EASA/inputs/inputs.json` [D+Y]. "One point out" = one latch point not engaged, the others fine. 100 000 simulated flights per cell. Assumption [Y]: a common linkage (partial lock affects all points together) and the same per-flight hazard rates on every type.

| Latch points | Architecture | P(miss \| partial) | P(miss \| one point out) | RF, pilot acts | RF, pilot matches |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Seated sensor only | 1 | 1 | 1.0× | 1.0× |
| 1 | Seated + one latch sensor | 0.00076 | 0.00076 | 1 327× | 3.0× |
| 1 | One sensor per latch point | 0.00076 | 0.00076 | 1 327× | 3.0× |
| 2 | Seated sensor only | 1 | 1 | 1.0× | 1.0× |
| 2 | Seated + one latch sensor | 0.00077 | 0.5 | 13.1× | 2.5× |
| 2 | One sensor per latch point | 0.00054 | 0.00054 | 1 868× | 3.0× |
| 3 | Seated sensor only | 1 | 1 | 1.0× | 1.0× |
| 3 | Seated + one latch sensor | 0.00082 | 0.67 | 9.8× | 2.3× |
| 3 | One sensor per latch point | 0.00055 | 0.0006 | 1 809× | 3.0× |
| 4 | Seated sensor only | 1 | 1 | 1.0× | 1.0× |
| 4 | Seated + one latch sensor | 0.00058 | 0.75 | 8.8× | 2.3× |
| 4 | One sensor per latch point | 0.00062 | 0.00057 | 1 647× | 3.0× |
| 5 | Seated sensor only | 1 | 1 | 1.0× | 1.0× |
| 5 | Seated + one latch sensor | 0.00059 | 0.8 | 8.2× | 2.3× |
| 5 | One sensor per latch point | 0.00048 | 0.00056 | 2 049× | 3.0× |

**Reading [K]:** a seated ("closed") sensor never sees a partial lock or a missing point, on any type. One latch sensor sees the partial lock (all points move together) but misses a single point out with probability (N − 1)/N. Only one sensor per latch point keeps the miss rate at the rigging-error floor for every N. So the rule for any aircraft is: **one engagement sensor per latch point plus one seated sensor**; the parts count grows with N, the logic does not change. Under probability matching every architecture is limited to a few times by the nuisance rate, as on the Extra NG.

**Cross-check [K]:** the 3-point rows must reproduce the Extra NG study (`02_EASA/outputs/day/result.json`: A2 9.9×, A3 1 901× with 200 000 flights, 95 % lower bound 1 568×) within Monte Carlo noise; here 9.8× and 1 809× with 100 000 flights per cell.

**For a new type, measure first (step 2):** number of latch points, whether they share one linkage, handle or pin travel between partial and full engagement, free space for a sensor within its sensing range at each point, and whether an open-and-released canopy reads like a locked one at the handle.
